headline: Avoiding Pitfalls in Your Home Addition Project
articleBody:
Embarking on a home addition is a big undertaking, and like any complex project, there are common missteps that can cause headaches and delays. One of the biggest mistakes we see is homeowners starting construction before all the necessary approvals are in place. Seriously, don't do it! It can lead to costly rework and even fines. Another frequent issue is overlooking critical zoning requirements like setback lines or lot coverage limits. These aren't just suggestions; they’re rules that determine how much of your property you can build on and where, and ignoring them will definitely lead to problems down the road. Plus, it's easy to submit incomplete plans, which means more back-and-forth with the city and extended timelines.

**Common Mistakes to Avoid**

Beyond the initial planning and permits, coordination is key. Failing to properly coordinate structural, HVAC, plumbing, and electrical requirements can lead to big headaches. Imagine having your new walls up only to find out there's no way to run the necessary plumbing or wiring efficiently! It's also super common to underestimate the challenge of seamlessly tying the new addition into your existing structure. You want it to look and feel like it was always meant to be there, not like an afterthought. Lastly, incomplete or noncompliant plans are a guaranteed way to get correction notices and resubmission requests, which slows everything down.
